question: I create a VkFramebuffer with flags = 0 for a render pass whose only subpass has viewMask 0b0110 and one color attachment. layers is 1, width and height equal the image extent, and the color VkImageView is a 2D array view of mip 0 with layerCount 2, matching format, samples and COLOR_ATTACHMENT usage. Is this valid?
reference_answer: No. With non-zero view masks in renderPass, every color, input, depth/stencil or resolve attachment view in pAttachments needs a layerCount exceeding the highest set bit index of those view masks. viewMask 0b0110 has its highest bit at index 2, so the color view needs at least 3 layers, and layerCount 2 is too few.
notes: Imageless flag not set, layers = 1 (multiview requires 1), layerCount 2 >= layers; only the view-mask layer rule is violated.

question: I'm creating a regular (not imageless) framebuffer for a render pass using multiple views; its single subpass renders views 1 and 2 and writes one color attachment. The framebuffer has one layer and matches the image size, and the color view covers mip 0 and two array layers with matching format, sample count and color-attachment usage. Is this valid?
reference_answer: No. When renderPass uses non-zero view masks, each color, input, depth/stencil or resolve attachment view in pAttachments needs a layerCount larger than the index of the highest bit set in those masks. Views 1 and 2 give a highest bit index of 2, so the view must have at least 3 layers; 2 layers violate the rule.
notes: Imageless flag not set, layers = 1 (multiview requires 1), layerCount 2 >= layers; only the view-mask layer rule is violated.

question: For vkCmdBeginRendering I pass a VkRenderingInfo with flags = 0, viewMask 0, layerCount 1, no depth or stencil attachment, and one color attachment: a 4-sample UNORM view in COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL with resolveMode = VK_RESOLVE_MODE_CUSTOM_BIT_EXT and a single-sampled resolveImageView of the same format and layout. customResolve is enabled and renderArea fits. What's wrong?
reference_answer: Because an attachment's resolveMode contains VK_RESOLVE_MODE_CUSTOM_BIT_EXT, VkRenderingInfo::flags has to include VK_RENDERING_CUSTOM_RESOLVE_BIT_EXT; with flags = 0 the structure is invalid. This applies to any color, depth or stencil attachment that uses the custom resolve mode.
notes: Non-integer color format allows CUSTOM resolve; flag not set so the customResolve-feature and flag-dependent rules do not apply.

question: I begin dynamic rendering with no rendering flags set, a single layer, no multiview and no depth or stencil attachment. The one color attachment is a 4x multisampled normalized color view in the color-attachment layout, resolved with the custom resolve mode into a single-sampled view of the same format and layout. Custom resolve support is enabled and the render area fits. What's wrong?
reference_answer: When any color, depth or stencil attachment uses VK_RESOLVE_MODE_CUSTOM_BIT_EXT as its resolveMode, VkRenderingInfo::flags has to include VK_RENDERING_CUSTOM_RESOLVE_BIT_EXT. Here no flags are set, so the custom resolve flag is missing and the rendering info is invalid.
notes: Non-integer color format allows CUSTOM resolve; flag not set so the customResolve-feature and flag-dependent rules do not apply.

question: I fill a VkShaderCreateInfoEXT with stage = VK_SHADER_STAGE_GEOMETRY_BIT to make a geometry shader object, but I did not enable the geometryShader feature on the device. What is required for this to be valid?
reference_answer: VkShaderCreateInfoEXT::stage must not be VK_SHADER_STAGE_GEOMETRY_BIT unless the geometryShader feature is enabled; to create a geometry-stage shader object you have to enable geometryShader.
notes: Question is about the stage member itself; the nextStage geometry rule is a different member.

question: I want to create a standalone shader object for the geometry stage, but the device was created without turning on geometry shader support. What is required for this to be valid?
reference_answer: A shader object whose stage is VK_SHADER_STAGE_GEOMETRY_BIT may only be created when the geometryShader feature is enabled; without that feature, VkShaderCreateInfoEXT::stage cannot be the geometry stage.
notes: Question is about the stage member itself; the nextStage geometry rule is a different member.

question: In a host vkBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR call with mode VK_BUILD_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_MODE_UPDATE_KHR, one VK_GEOMETRY_TYPE_TRIANGLES_KHR geometry had a non-NULL geometry.triangles.transformData when srcAccelerationStructure was last built. Can I pass a NULL transformData for that geometry in this update?
reference_answer: No. In an update, if a triangle geometry's geometry.triangles.transformData address was non-NULL in the last build of srcAccelerationStructure, it must be non-NULL in the update as well.

question: I'm updating an acceleration structure on the host. One of its triangle geometries used a transform matrix address when the source structure was last built. Is it allowed to drop the transform, passing a null address, for that geometry in the update?
reference_answer: No. For VK_BUILD_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_MODE_UPDATE_KHR, a VK_GEOMETRY_TYPE_TRIANGLES_KHR geometry whose transformData was non-NULL when srcAccelerationStructure was last built must keep a non-NULL transformData in the update.

question: I record vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresIndirectKHR with infoCount = 1 (BUILD mode, bottom-level triangles). One 2 MiB buffer with all required usages holds dstAccelerationStructure at offset 0 with size 512 KiB (large enough), and scratchData.deviceAddress is the buffer address + 256 KiB, correctly aligned with the scratch range inside the buffer. Everything else is valid. What's wrong?
reference_answer: The memory backing dstAccelerationStructure that the build accesses must be disjoint from the memory backing scratchData of every element of pInfos, its own element included. Scratch starting at 256 KiB lies inside the acceleration structure's 0-512 KiB range, so the two overlap.
notes: Single element, BUILD mode, so the other-element and source-structure overlap rules do not apply.

question: I record an indirect, device-side build of one bottom-level triangle acceleration structure. I suballocate a 2-megabyte buffer with all needed usages: the destination structure sits at offset 0 with a size of 512 kilobytes (enough), and the scratch address points to offset 256 kilobytes, correctly aligned, with the scratch range inside the buffer. Everything else is valid. What's wrong?
reference_answer: The destination acceleration structure's memory accessed by vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresIndirectKHR must not overlap the scratch memory (scratchData) of any build in the call, including its own. Scratch at offset 256 KiB falls within the destination's 0-512 KiB range, so they overlap.
notes: Single element, BUILD mode, so the other-element and source-structure overlap rules do not apply.

question: When I build an opacity micromap with vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR, setting pInfos[i].type to VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_KHR, which VkAccelerationStructureCreateInfoKHR::type values are acceptable for the object I pass as dstAccelerationStructure?
reference_answer: If pInfos[i].type is VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_KHR, dstAccelerationStructure has to be an object whose VkAccelerationStructureCreateInfoKHR::type at creation was either VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_KHR or VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_GENERIC_KHR.

question: I'm recording a device-side build of an opacity micromap. What type must the destination acceleration structure object have been given when I created it?
reference_answer: For a build whose type is VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_KHR, the dstAccelerationStructure has to have been created with VkAccelerationStructureCreateInfoKHR::type equal to VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_OPACITY_MICROMAP_KHR or VK_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_TYPE_GENERIC_KHR.

question: I build a micromap with vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR by chaining a VkAccelerationStructureGeometryMicromapDataKHR into the geometry's pNext. What usage must the buffers behind its data and triangleArray device addresses have been created with?
reference_answer: When a geometry's pNext chain includes VkAccelerationStructureGeometryMicromapDataKHR, the buffers whose device addresses are used for its data and triangleArray members need VK_BUFFER_USAGE_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_BUILD_INPUT_READ_ONLY_BIT_KHR in their creation usage.

question: When recording a device build of a micromap, I supply device addresses for the micromap's raw data and for its per-triangle descriptor array. What buffer usage must the buffers those addresses come from have been created with?
reference_answer: The buffers from which the data and triangleArray addresses of VkAccelerationStructureGeometryMicromapDataKHR are obtained need VK_BUFFER_USAGE_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_BUILD_INPUT_READ_ONLY_BIT_KHR in their creation usage.
